title: Affine approximation from a large squared coefficient
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:\mathbb F_2^n\to\mathbb F_2$, and let $t\in\mathbb R$. Suppose some $\gamma\in\mathbb F_2^n$ has squared vector Fourier coefficient of the real sign encoding of $f$ at least $t$. Then there are $b\in\mathbb F_2$ and $\gamma'\in\mathbb F_2^n$ such that the uniform average of the product of the sign encodings of $f$ and the affine function $x\mapsto b+\gamma'\cdot x$ is at least $\sqrt t$, and their relative Hamming distance is at most $1/2-\sqrt t/2$.
hypotheses_covered: Some vector Fourier coefficient of the real sign encoding of $f$ has square at least $t$
